item.title: Federated Graph Learning for EV Charging Demand Forecasting with Personalization Against Cyberattacks
item.description:
IEEE Transactions on Intelligent Transportation Systems · Yi Li, Renyou Xie, Chaojie Li, Yi Wang, Zhaoyang Dong
Mitigating cybersecurity risk in electric vehicle (EV) charging demand forecasting plays a crucial role in the safe operation of collective EV chargings, the stability of the power grid, and the cost-effective infrastructure expansion. However, existing methods either suffer from the data privacy issue and the susceptibility to cyberattacks or fail to consider the spatial correlation among different stations. To address these challenges, a federated graph learning approach involving multiple charging stations is proposed to collaboratively train a more generalized deep learning model for demand forecasting while capturing spatial correlations among various stations and enhancing robustness against potential attacks. Firstly, for better model performance, a Graph Neural Network (GNN) model is leveraged to characterize the geographic correlation among different charging stations in a federated manner. Secondly, to ensure robustness and deal with the data heterogeneity in a federated setting, a message passing that utilizes a global attention mechanism to aggregate personalized models for each client is proposed. Thirdly, by concerning cyberattacks, a special credit-based function is designed to mitigate potential threats from malicious clients or unwanted attacks. Extensive experiments on a public EV charging dataset are conducted using various deep learning techniques and federated learning methods to demonstrate the prediction accuracy and robustness of the proposed approach.

item.title: Ampere: Communication-Efficient and High-Accuracy Split Federated Learning
item.description:
IEEE Transactions on Parallel and Distributed Systems · Zihan Zhang, Leon Wong, Blesson Varghese
A Federated Learning (FL) system collaboratively trains neural networks across devices and a server but is limited by significant on-device computation costs. Split Federated Learning (SFL) systems mitigate this by offloading a block of layers of the network from the device to a server. However, in doing so, it introduces large communication overheads due to frequent exchanges of intermediate activations and gradients between devices and the server and reduces model accuracy for non-IID data. We propose Ampere, a novel collaborative training system that simultaneously minimizes on-device computation and device-server communication while improving model accuracy. Unlike SFL, which uses a global loss by iterative end-to-end training, Ampere develops unidirectional inter-block training to sequentially train the device and server blocks with a local loss, eliminating the transfer of gradients. A lightweight auxiliary network generation method decouples training between the device and server, reducing frequent intermediate exchanges to a single transfer, which significantly reduces the communication overhead. Ampere mitigates the impact of data heterogeneity by consolidating activations generated by the trained device block to train the server block, in contrast to SFL, which trains on device-specific, non-IID activations. Extensive experiments on multiple CNNs and Transformers show that, compared to state-of-the-art SFL baseline systems, Ampere (i) improves model accuracy by up to 11.70 percentage points while training up to 18.6x faster, (ii) incurs up to 911x lower device-server communication overhead and up to 14.5x lower on-device computation, and (iii) reduces standard deviation of accuracy by 71.13% for various non-IID degrees highlighting superior performance when faced with heterogeneous data. Ampere is available from https://github.com/blessonvar/Ampere.

item.title: Personalized Federated Learning for Multiple Tasks in Internet of Vehicles
item.description:
IEEE Transactions on Intelligent Transportation Systems · Yuchuan Fu, Bingqing Li, Xinlong Tang, Changle Li, Fei Richard Yu, Nan Cheng
Federated learning (FL) has emerged as a key technology for collaborative perception and decision-making in vehicular networks, owing to its distributed architecture and privacy-preserving characteristics. Nevertheless, three critical challenges hinder FL deployment in Internet of Vehicles (IoV) scenarios: concurrent execution of multiple tasks, weak cross-task correlations, and negative transfer effects. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a personalized multi-task FL algorithm featuring edge-assisted aggregation and hierarchical training. Specifically, we first decentralize the aggregation process through CAV edge nodes, establishing a hierarchical training architecture that achieves joint optimization through shared feature extraction layers and task-specific decision layers. Next, we develop a representation similarity-aware weighting algorithm to mitigate negative transfer during global model aggregation. Extensive simulation results demonstrate that the proposed algorithm significantly improves model accuracy and convergence speed while reducing energy and time cost in multi-task IoV scenarios.

item.title: Taming Staleness in Asynchronous Federated Learning With System Heterogeneity
item.description:
IEEE Transactions on Parallel and Distributed Systems · Zhenhao Liu, Mengyao Li, Bo Zhang, Xiaozhu Liu, Rongbo Zhu
Asynchronous federated learning is a distributed machine learning framework designed for parallel and distributed systems. However, system heterogeneity in communication and computation can cause stragglers to upload stale updates, which may degrade the performance of the global model. Existing studies primarily focus on systems with mild to moderate heterogeneity, leaving the trade-off between communication efficiency and model performance insufficiently addressed in extreme scenarios. To tackle this issue, we propose FedASRA, an efficient semi-asynchronous federated learning framework featuring adaptive alternating selection (AAS) and real-time staleness adjustment (RSA). Specifically, AAS leverages a multi-attribute utility function to periodically schedule the participation of stragglers and fast clients in an alternating manner, thereby narrowing the system heterogeneity gap among clients in each communication round. When staleness is unavoidable, RSA enables stragglers to synchronously receive the latest global model during training and compute updated gradients. These updated gradients are then locally aggregated with the soon-to-be stale gradients to improve the freshness of submitted updates. We provide convergence and system complexity analysis for FedASRA, establishing a staleness-agnostic convergence upper bound. Extensive experiments are conducted in simulated environments and a prototype system built with 21 real-world devices. Results demonstrate that FedASRA achieves a favorable balance between system efficiency and performance. Compared with state-of-the-art methods, FedASRA reduces wall-clock time by 18.51% and communication overhead by 11.66% on average.

item.title: A Bio-Inspired Hierarchical Federated Learning Framework With Joint Computing Communication Control Optimization for Green UAV Inspection
item.description:
IEEE Transactions on Parallel and Distributed Systems · Tianle Xia, Haitao Zhao, Miao Liu, Jie Yang, Chun Zhu, Hongbo Zhu
With the development of UAV communications and aerial edge intelligence, Uncrewed Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) are increasingly used for inspection in high-risk environments. However, limited onboard energy and data-privacy constraints make efficient collaborative learning challenging. Hierarchical Federated Learning (HFL) provides a privacy-preserving paradigm, yet existing energy-optimization studies often treat computing, communication, and client selection separately, lacking a unified system perspective. Inspired by biological neural systems, where neurons compute in an event-driven manner, synapses transmit information sparsely, and organisms make reward-modulated decisions, we propose a Bio-Inspired Hierarchical Federated Learning (BIO-HFL) framework that takes UAV energy consumption as the central driving objective. In the computation module, BIO-HFL employs Spiking Neural Networks (SNNs) to realize neuron-like event-driven computing and reduce onboard energy; in the communication module, it integrates a Critical Tensor mechanism into Deep Gradient Compression (DGC-CT) to mimic synapse-like sparse but selective transmission and maintain stability under high compression ratios; and in the control module, it uses a Distributed Multi-Armed Bandit (DMAB) strategy as an organism-level decision module to select clients with minimal expected energy consumption. These three components are mutually coupled, SNN and DGC-CT energy statistics serve as inputs to DMAB, DMAB determines the optimization targets of SNN and DGC-CT through energy-aware scheduling, and CT selection in DGC-CT further depends on SNN-driven spike distributions. Experiments demonstrate that DGC-CT ensures stable training even at a 10% compression ratio, and DMAB reduces inefficient client participation. Across both CIFAR-10 and DAGM2007, BIO-HFL consistently improves energy efficiency while maintaining competitive macro-average F1, achieving up to 81.1% lower total energy consumption compared with a conventional SNN-HFL baseline.

item.title: TS-FL: A Two-Stage Federated Learning Framework for Zero-Day Attack Detection in Autonomous Vehicle CAN-FD Networks
item.description:
IEEE Transactions on Intelligent Transportation Systems · Wenting Lu, Ayong Ye, Yuanhuang Liu, Longjing Yang, Puning Zhao, Zhiquan Liu
The development of autonomous vehicles has exposed Controller Area Network with Flexible Data-Rate (CAN-FD) networks to growing zero-day threats: attacks that exploit undisclosed or unpatched vulnerabilities. Current machine learning-based attack detection systems are severely constrained by data isolation due to privacy requirements, and their relatively long detection times often lead to frame drops during peak traffic scenarios. To address these issues, we present a two-stage Federated Learning (FL) framework based on Extreme Gradient Boosting Decision Tree (XGBoost) for collaborative zero-day attack detection in vehicle networks. The framework combines privacy-preserving federated learning with efficient XGBoost models to achieve both data isolation compliance and efficient detection. Different from current methods, we follow a progressive filtering scheme. The first binary classification stage aims to filter as many anomalies as possible while keeping up with CAN data transmission; the second multi-classification stage targets to recognize unknown attacks while classifying known attacks precisely. The results show that our method comprehensively outperforms nearly all mainstream baseline approaches across all evaluation metrics and exceeds common unsupervised methods in zero-day attack detection. Under sustained 1 kHz CAN-FD traffic with a batch size of 100 frames, TS-FL achieves zero frame drops while other methods lose 0.5-12%. For strict frame-by-frame processing, our per-frame inference latency is comparable to that of CNN-based FL baselines. Our code is available athttps://github.com/deer-echo/Two-step-FL

item.title: Rethinking Objective Image Quality Assessment With Federated Learning
item.description:
IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems for Video Technology · Shishun Tian, Yonghong Zheng, Guanghui Yue, Weisi Lin, Patrick Le Callet
Deep neural network (DNN)-based image quality assessment (IQA) methods have achieved remarkable progress in recent years. However, existing DNN-based IQA approaches still face two major challenges. First, IQA datasets usually suffer from insufficient training samples. Second, substantial differences in quality scoring standards and scales among different datasets limit the unified training of IQA models. In this paper, we propose a novel objective IQA training framework based on federated learning (FL). To tackle the problem of insufficient labeled training samples, the proposed FL-based IQA framework conducts collaborative training by uniting samples from different datasets. Instead of simply mixing multiple datasets, we train the IQA model on each dataset individually and aggregate the results of different models. Meanwhile, considering the inconsistencies in the scoring standards and scales of different datasets, we propose a model decoupling strategy to divide the model into shared and personalized components: the former maintains global knowledge across all models, while the latter allows flexible adjustments tailored to the specific characteristics of individual datasets. Experiments on five IQA datasets show that our proposed FL-based IQA framework has improvements in accuracy and robustness on existing IQA models.

item.title: Rising From Embodied Intelligence to Embedded Intelligence via Decentralized Federated Learning With Roaming AI Agents
item.description:
IEEE/ASME Transactions on Mechatronics · Yicheng Di, Hongjian Shi, Bowen Jiang, Yingli Peng, Hongyu Zhao, Shuhui Zhou
Industrial inkjet printing platforms require embedded intelligence that tightly integrates sensing, actuation, control, and embedded computing under strict constraints on computation, memory, energy, and deterministic timing. However, privacy and compliance restrictions prevent raw data sharing, limiting the effectiveness of cloud-based learning. Federated learning addresses privacy concerns through model-update sharing, but centralized orchestration suffers from server bottlenecks and single-point failures, creating communication congestion and scalability limitations in industrial deployments. Decentralized federated learning removes the central server, yet synchronous all-neighbor aggregation remains vulnerable to stragglers and model divergence under heterogeneous and non-independent and identically distributed (non-IID) conditions. To address these challenges, we propose Rising from Embodied Intelligence to Embedded Intelligence via Decentralized Federated Learning with Roaming AI Agents (REEDFL), a decentralized federated learning framework with roaming AI agents for industrial embedded intelligence. Instead of global synchronization, roaming agents carry model states and perform hop-by-hop training across the peer topology, activating only agent-hosting nodes in each round. When multiple agents meet at a node, a consistency-preserving multiagent fusion module weights their states according to compatibility with local data, providing stable initialization for subsequent training. An intelligent scheduling mechanism further selects next hops by jointly considering data utility, resource availability, and forgetting signals. Experiments on a real five-node industrial inkjet platform show that REEDFL achieves faster convergence and up to 5.06% higher accuracy than the strongest baseline.

item.title: Service-Centric Adolescent Mental Health Early Warning Solutions and Enabling Technologies: Survey and Framework
item.description:
IEEE Transactions on Services Computing · Jiawei Dang, Jiali Zhu, Junyang Chen, Haodi Zhang, Liang‐Jie Zhang
The increasing global prevalence of adolescent mental health challenges demands proactive early warning systems. Although such systems have attracted growing research interest, most prior work emphasizes algorithmic performance, while the surrounding service infrastructure remains underexplored. To address key limitations in current practice, including data silos, insufficient multimodal data integration, and inadequate privacy protection during continuous model evolution, this paper presents a service-oriented, end-to-end framework for adolescent mental health early warning, in which data governance, modeling, and feedback are organized as interoperable microservices. The framework adopts a lakehouse architecture as a governed data layer that unifies multimodal schemas, data lineage, access control, and reusable analytics to facilitate cross-institution collaboration. Built upon this layer, we develop multimodal feature representations that integrate textual, visual, auditory, and physiological signals, together with a modular early warning service engine. To support continual refinement without exposing sensitive data, we further propose Dynamic Federated Co-Evolution (DFCE), a paradigm that couples cross-institutional federated learning with an expert-in-the-loop feedback mechanism, allowing models to co-evolve with expert feedback across institutions. As a proof of concept for the DFCE component, experiments on multimodal sentiment benchmarks show that DFCE maintains competitive predictive performance while enabling privacy-preserving collaboration under continual updates. We position these results as evidence of algorithmic and systems-level feasibility for privacy-preserving, cross-institutional collaboration, without claiming clinical diagnostic validity.

item.title: FBHS: A High-Performance Framework for Real-Time Task Scheduling on big.LITTLE Architectures
item.description:
IEEE Transactions on Sustainable Computing · Yayun Liang, Wufei Wu, Jiafeng Wang, Yan Xie
Heterogeneous multi-core processors (such as the ARM big.LITTLE architecture) have become the mainstream platform for edge computing and real-time embedded systems due to their dynamic trade-off between high performance and high energy efficiency. Currently, heterogeneous multi-core scheduling faces the challenge of collaboratively optimizing task execution time and system energy consumption. Existing methods have the problem of insufficient heterogeneous adaptability when dealing with tasks with complex dependencies. To address these challenges, this paper proposes an innovative Federated Bundled Hybrid Scheduling (FBHS) framework, which seamlessly combines federated and bundled scheduling through a dynamic selection mechanism guided by capacity enhancement bounds, alongside a differentiated resource allocation strategy tailored for high and low utilization tasks. Experimental results demonstrate that, in task scenarios ranging from 20 to 70 tasks, FBHS outperforms pure federated scheduling (PFS), pure bundled scheduling (PBS), completely fair scheduler (CFS), and evolutionary algorithm based heterogeneous earliest finish time (E-HEFT), achieving average reductions of 18.3%, 26.1%, 31.7%, and 10.10% in energy consumption and 45.8%, 50.95%, 56.2%, and 21.18% in execution time, respectively. Furthermore, the results were verified in real data streams such as Montage and CyberShake, highlighting the effectiveness of FBHS in simultaneously enhancing real-time performance and energy efficiency on heterogeneous multi-core architectures.

item.title: FedMGL: Boosting One-Shot Federated Learning via Mixture of Grouped LoRA Experts
item.description:
IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems for Video Technology · Ke Xu, Yue Wang, Y Zhang, Bo Xiao, Cuiqun Chen, Xingyi Zhang
Federated tuning methods typically involve full parameter fine-tuning and require multiple rounds of communication with the server. However, the communication budget resulting from fully fine-tuning is impractical in the real world. Combining the One-Shot FL paradigm and parameter-efficient fine-tuning methods, such as LoRA, can reduce the communication budget hundreds of times, but model aggregation performance will be seriously degraded and lacks robustness. Current OFL is typically based on full-parameter training, which hinders the practical application of OFL. Based on the LoRA trained via OFL, we propose a method by boosting One-ShotFederated tuning withMixture ofGroupedLoRAs calledFedMGLthat significantly improves performance without training the LoRA parameters themselves. To reduce communication and training overhead, FedMGL first performs similarity grouping and aggregation for the locally trained LoRA matrix. To achieve learnable aggregation, we freeze the grouped LoRA modules and locally fine-tune gating units on the client or server side, requiring minimal training overhead. Additionally, it learns better aggregation ratios, making the final aggregated parameters more robust. Extensive experiments show that FedMGL has superior performance on various settings without compromising data privacy or incurring large communication costs.

item.title: Federated Aggregation of Full Mallows Rankings via Borda and Lehmer Coding
item.description:
IEEE Transactions on Information Theory · Jin Sima, Vishal Rana, Olgica Milenković
Rank aggregation (RA) is the process of merging different rankings into a single representative consensus order. In applications involving personal data sharing and analysis, rankings are stored at physically distributed locations and have to be kept private. This motivates the study offederated rank aggregation protocolsthat enable secure and communication-efficient learning using multiple local ranking repositories. Here we describe the first known collection of provably efficient approaches for federated rank aggregation that utilize Borda scoring and Lehmer codes and enable low data processing/exchange costs via rank quantization. Our main results are rigorous sample and communication complexity characterizations of federated algorithms for Mallows distributions withunknowncentroid permutation$\sigma _{0}$andunknownscaling factor$\phi $. The findings reveal that under certain mild conditions, our federated protocols have the same order of sample complexity as centralized methods. We also present experimental results on synthetic and real-world ranking data, such as Sushi preferences, Jester, two prioritized Landmark gene expression datasets and votes from the Primary Maine Governor Election 2018.

item.title: BIPPO: Budget-Aware Independent PPO for Energy-Efficient Federated Learning Services
item.description:
IEEE Transactions on Services Computing · Anna Lackinger, Andrea Morichetta, Pantelis A. Frangoudis, Schahram Dustdar
Federated Learning (FL) is a promising machine learning solution in large-scale IoT systems, guaranteeing load distribution and privacy. However, FL does not natively consider infrastructure efficiency, a critical concern for systems operating in resource-constrained environments. Several Reinforcement Learning (RL) based solutions offer improved client selection for FL; however, they do not consider infrastructure challenges, such as resource limitations and device churn. Furthermore, the training of RL methods is often not designed for practical application, as these approaches frequently do not consider generalizability and are not optimized for energy efficiency. To fill this gap, we propose BIPPO (Budget-aware Independent Proximal Policy Optimization), which is an energy-efficient multi-agent RL solution that improves performance. We evaluate BIPPO on two image classification tasks run in a highly budget-constrained setting, with FL clients training on non-IID data, a challenging context for vanilla FL. The improved sampler of BIPPO enables it to increase the mean accuracy compared to non-RL mechanisms, traditional PPO, and IPPO. In addition, BIPPO only consumes a negligible proportion of the budget, which stays consistent even if the number of clients increases. Overall, BIPPO delivers a performant, stable, scalable, and sustainable solution for client selection in IoT-FL.

item.title: FedRepu: A Reputation-Based Aggregation Strategy for Federated Learning in Bearing Fault Diagnosis
item.description:
IEEE Transactions on Industrial Informatics · Junxian You, Rui Yang, Zidong Wang
Integrating federated learning in bearing fault diagnosis marks a crucial step in industrial operations, showing great potential for enhancing diagnostic accuracy and data privacy. However, the effectiveness of federated learning is often compromised by varying data quality and quantity among clients. FedRepu, a novel reputation-based aggregation strategy for federated learning in bearing fault diagnosis, is introduced in this article by employing an extended reputation mechanism that scores client trustworthiness based on real-time, historical, and rewarding performance metrics, dynamically adapting model aggregation to quality of contributions. It deals with natural heterogeneity in distributed sources and improves performance uniformly across clients. Comprehensive experiments on the Case Western Reserve University, Paderborn University, and Huazhong University of Science and Technology datasets, including comparison studies of cross-validation tasks and ablation studies, confirm FedRepu's effectiveness in improving model aggregation efficiency despite reputation discrepancies. Sensitivity analysis further demonstrates its robustness to hyperparameter variations, making FedRepu a promising solution for federated learning in bearing fault diagnosis.

item.title: MAFEE: Mobility-Aware Hierarchical Federated Learning With EC-MARL for Edge Caching in Internet of Vehicles
item.description:
IEEE Transactions on Intelligent Transportation Systems · Mengmeng Shao, Xiaoheng Deng, Jingjing Zhang, Zhenyang Shu, Jinsong Gui, Geyong Min
To support rapidly increasing services from vehicle users (VUs), such as short videos, in-car entertainment, etc., edge caching has emerged as a critical proposal to enable more efficient content delivery and low-latency services in Internet of Vehicles (IoVs). Due to the conflict of a massive amount of content and limited Roadside Unit (RSU) resources, edge caching optimization is crucial to the effective utilization of the caching resources in IoVs. Consequently, we integrate recommender systems and efficient cache replacement to optimize edge caching. Specifically, rapid spatiotemporal dynamics of content popularity due to vehicles mobility and non-uniform vehicle density within an RSU’s coverage pose significant challenges for RSU local model to predict content popularity accurately. Therefore, considering vehicles’ heterogeneous resources and local model similarity, we propose a Mobility-Aware Hierarchical Federated Learning (MAHFL) popularity prediction framework, equipped with an adaptive aggregation update mechanism for weighting factors. Additionally, based on content popularity prediction and considering the tidal flow phenomenon of vehicular traffic, we propose a double-memory Episodic Control Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (EC-MARL) with multiple timescales that incorporates both instantaneous environmental changes and long-term regularities. The proposed scheme MAFEE, an innovative framework that synergistically combines MAHFL and EC-MARL, effectively addresses the critical challenges of highly dynamic environment, significant node heterogeneity, and content diversity, thereby enabling highly efficient caching of popular content in IoVs. Extensive simulations on real-world dataset demonstrate that our framework outperforms baseline schemes, efficiently improving the cache hit rate and reducing the latency for content delivery.

item.title: FedNereus: Incentive-Aware Heterogeneous Federated Learning Under Resource Constraint
item.description:
IEEE Transactions on Computers · Fuyuan Xia, Chenhao Ying, Xikun Jiang, Weiting Zhang, Haiming Jin, Jie Li
As public concern about data privacy continues to grow, federated learning (FL), as a machine learning technique that does not require the disclosure of user raw data, has attracted widespread attention. However, it still has many common problems. The first problem stems from the absence of incentive mechanisms utilized to incentivize more participation to improve the performance of learning models. The second problem arises from the limited resources of mobile devices that can be utilized for model training, which will seriously decrease the performance of learning models. To address the aforementioned issues, in this paper, we propose a novel incentive-aware collaborative construction of heterogeneous Federated learNing under resource constraint, namely FedNereus. In fact, FedNereus enables to incentivize more participation to participate in model training by applying an auction-based incentive mechanism. It is proved that FedNereus allows participating workers to report their actual cost as their bidding price, which is referred to as truthfulness. Furthermore, it also allows workers to obtain non-negative reward, which is also referred to as the individual rationality. In order to break the resource limitation, FedNereus meticulously designs the rules of model selection so that workers can only train a portion of the learning model based on their limited hardware capabilities, while maintaining the performance guarantee of learning models. The excess empirical risk of FedNereus is shown to be upper bounded by O(1/T), where T is the number of training rounds. Finally, extensive experiments are conducted, whose results show that FedNereus outperforms state-of-the-art approaches in different learning tasks.

item.title: HierSat: Hierarchical Aggregation for Latency-Efficient Federated Learning in Satellite Networks
item.description:
IEEE Transactions on Computers · Jian Zhou, Wenkai Ji, Yue Wang, Anfeng Liu, Qian He, Fu Xiao
The global coverage of low Earth orbit (LEO) satellites creates a natural platform for distributed intelligence, but privacy risks caused by massive transmission of raw remote sensing data pose critical challenges. To address this, federated learning (FL) has become a promising distributed learning framework for satellite networks, which exchanges only model parameters instead of raw data. However, most existing frameworks fail to fully exploit the structure of the satellite networks. Some work using ground stations (GSs) as parameter servers (PS) cannot handle large model parameter transmission due to limited communication windows between LEO satellites and GSs, while others do not effectively use inter-satellite links (ISL) for global model aggregation, thus resulting in significant training latency. Different from existing frameworks, this paper proposes ahierarchical FL framework forsatellite networks,HierSat, which strategically leverages the persistent wide-area coverage and stable energy supply of geostationary Earth orbit (GEO) satellites for continuous model synchronization, while harnessing high-speed ISLs to enable direct satellite coordination. Meanwhile, to efficiently leverage the ring communication topology of LEO orbits, the Ring All-Reduce algorithm is adopted for model aggregation. Furthermore, a joint optimization problem addressing master satellite selection, computation resource allocation, and quantization bits is formulated to minimize per-round latency under energy constraints and accuracy requirements. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness ofHierSatin DNN based classification tasks under satellite networks.

item.title: Quantum Federated Learning: A Comprehensive Review and Analysis
item.description:
IEEE Transactions on Artificial Intelligence · Dev Gurung, Shiva Raj Pokhrel, Gang Li
This article presents a comprehensive review and empirical analysis of quantum federated learning (QFL), an emerging interdisciplinary field integrating quantum machine learning (QML) with federated learning. Driven by the growing capabilities of quantum computing (QC) and the various challenges in classical federated learning (CFL) such as computational capacity, handling large-scale distributed data, etc., we examine the theoretical foundations, methodological developments, and practical challenges of QFL. Our work systematically examines the existing literature, categorizes existing QFL approaches, and assesses their applicability across diverse domains. Leveraging major quantum platforms including Qiskit, PennyLane, and TensorCircuit, we conduct extensive experiments on both simulators and real IBM quantum hardware. We provide comprehensive literature review, extensive experimental analysis showcasing significant discrepancies such as between simulated and real-hardware results, impact of heterogeneity, platform specific limitations with multiple ablation studies examining impact of noise, quantum classifier, simulators, etc. We conclude with discussions on various insights that identify open research challenges and outline future directions for scalable and reliable QFL integration with next-generation technologies.

item.title: Mitigating Generator Bias in Low-Participation Model-Heterogeneous Federated Learning
item.description:
IEEE Transactions on Artificial Intelligence · J B Chen, Yiting Zheng, Bohan Lin, Haozhe Cheng, Qinghai Zheng, Zhu J
Model heterogeneity and limited client participation are two defining challenges in real-world federated learning (FL). Representative generator-based distillation methods use a server-side generator to synthesize pseudo-data for knowledge aggregation. However, under sparse participation, the generator suffers from biased supervision, overfitting to frequent participants and overlooking rarely seen clients, which we refer to asgenerator bias. To address this, we propose Federated LEarning with Debiased GEnerator (FLEdge), a unified framework that mitigates generator bias and supports robust personalization under heterogeneous models. FLEdge introduces debiased knowledge distillation (DKD), which reweights both client- and sample-level contributions during distillation to correct distributional imbalance and guide the generator toward more comprehensive pseudo-data. To further enhance downstream personalization, we propose bidirectional contrastive personalization (BCP), which decomposes local models into encoders and classifiers, enabling contrastive alignment with global features and temporal consistency with past decision boundaries. Extensive experiments on popular benchmarks show that FLEdge consistently improves low-participation model-heterogeneous FL, achieving up to$\mathbf{3.86\%}$absolute accuracy gains over the best competing baseline on Tiny-ImageNet. Diagnostic analysis further shows that DKD reduces the empirical distillation loss gap from 1.239 to 1.084, providing empirical diagnostic evidence of reduced generator bias.

item.title: FedCon 2 : Federated Learning on Non-I.I.D. Continual Data via Dual-Contrastive Representations
item.description:
IEEE Transactions on Systems Man and Cybernetics Systems · Hang Yang, Zhiwu Li, Witold Pedrycz C
Federated learning (FL) is a promising paradigm for training a shared global model on decentralized data distributed across multiple clients while preserving data privacy. In practical scenarios, client-side data are often nonstationary and exhibit time-varying distributions. As a result, the global model may suffer from catastrophic forgetting, where knowledge acquired from earlier tasks is degraded when learning new ones. To address continual learning in federated settings, we propose FedCon2, a dual-contrastive representation learning framework. To mitigate forgetting, representative instances from previous tasks are selected and replayed during current training. Since contrastive learning benefits from diverse samples, a determinantal point process (DPP) is adopted to improve the memory sampling strategy. FedCon2performs contrastive learning at both intraclient and interclient levels, enabling each client to jointly learn new tasks while retaining prior knowledge at both data and model levels. In addition, model-level contrastive learning aligns local models with the global model to alleviate the impact of non-independent and identically distributed (non-I.I.D.) data across clients. The experimental results on three continual FL (CFL) settings demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms representative baselines.

item.title: Privacy-Preserving Coordination of Heterogeneous Electrolyzers: A Federated Reinforcement Learning Approach With Safety Guarantees
item.description:
IEEE Transactions on Sustainable Energy · Wenzhi Yang, Sheng Chen, Manyun Huang, Zhengmao Li, Edris Pouresmaeil, Zhinong Wei
The complementarity between high-flexibility Proton Exchange Membrane (PEM) and low-cost Alkaline (ALK) electrolyzers contributes to the synergistic development of green power and hydrogen sectors. However, wide-range renewable power fluctuations impose technical challenges on the optimal power allocation among these heterogeneous PEM and ALK units, which might result in safety violations and operational inefficiency. To address these challenges, this study proposes a privacy-preserving, physics-informed federated multi-agent control framework. Specifically, the architecture leverages a federated learning paradigm to aggregate decentralized strategies with limited direct data exchange, while incorporating an LSTM-enhanced algorithm to resolve partial observability by tracking long-timescale multiphysics dynamics like thermodynamic evolution and gas purity. Furthermore, a dual-tier proactive defense mechanism integrating a robust risk predictor with a quadratic programming projection layer is designed to strictly enforce hard physical constraints. Numerical results verify that the proposed approach effectively balances data privacy, physical safety, and precise regulation performance.

item.title: FedGMI: Generative Model-Driven Federated Learning for Probabilistic Mixture Inference
item.description:
IEEE Transactions on Artificial Intelligence · Qijun Hou, Y Shi, Pingyi Fan, Khaled B. Letaief
Federated Learning (FL) facilitates collaborative model training across decentralized clients while preserving data privacy by avoiding raw data exchange. Despite its potential, FL performance is often compromised by data heterogeneity across clients. To address this, Clustered Federated Learning (CFL) groups clients with similar data distributions to improve model performance, but constrained by intra-cluster heterogeneity. Conversely, Personalized Federated Learning (PFL) tailors models to individual clients, but usually neglects the underlying structural similarities among clients. In this work, we investigate a probabilistic mixture (PM) scenario, where each client's local data distribution is modeled as a convex combination of several shared inherent distributions. To effectively model this structure, we propose FedGMI, a framework that utilizes Variational Autoencoders (VAEs) as generative density estimators to represent these inherent distributions and infer the mixture components of clients' local data distributions. This approach enables structured personalization without sacrificing the benefits of collaborative learning. Extensive experiments demonstrate that FedGMI effectively characterizes and discriminate the inherent distributions, as well as accurately estimates mixture proportions. Furthermore, FedGMI maintains robust performance even under communication cost constraints.

item.title: Blockchain-Assisted Reliable Federated Learning in 5G-Powered Vehicular Systems
item.description:
IEEE Transactions on Intelligent Transportation Systems · Marcell Szabó, László Toka
The transformation of transport systems increasingly relies on connecting vehicles into cooperative networks, promising to reduce traffic congestion, lower emissions, and enhance road safety. Achieving these benefits requires efficient sharing of high definition (HD) map information across vehicles. Federated learning (FL) enables vehicles to collaboratively train shared models for HD maps, supporting accurate localization and dynamic environment understanding, without transferring raw data, thus preserving privacy. However, implementing FL in this context faces significant challenges: malicious participants can disrupt learning, and honest participants may disengage without sufficient incentives. To address these issues, we propose integrating a dual blockchain framework with FL, which evaluates participant reliability, weights contributions accordingly, and provides financial incentives to maintain engagement. This coordinated approach ensures that only trustworthy information contributes to HD map updates, preserving both data privacy and system integrity. By modeling and optimizing the system’s economic utility, and validating through simulations, we demonstrate that the framework is feasible under realistic settings when reward and subscription fees are appropriately calibrated, providing a robust foundation for secure, incentivized, and privacy preserving vehicular networks.

item.title: FedHarmony: A Unified Framework for Addressing Clinical Heterogeneity in Federated Medical Image Analysis
item.description:
IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems for Video Technology · Haoyu Mao, Tengfei Cao, Y. B. Liu, Han Xiao, Changqiao Xu
Federated Learning (FL) offers a privacy-preserving approach for collaborative modeling of federated medical imaging data across multiple centers. However, clinical heterogeneity, which arises from differences in imaging equipment, scanning protocols, and patient populations across centers, leads to performance drift and limits the model’s global generalization. Existing methods typically optimize client selection and model aggregation separately, which makes it difficult to mitigate the combined negative effects of unrepresentative training queues and unstable model fusion. In this study, we propose FedHarmony, a unified framework designed to address clinical heterogeneity in federated medical image analysis. The focus of this work is heterogeneity-aware federated learning for multi-center medical imaging, where variations in imaging quality, acquisition conditions, and patient distributions may jointly impair robustness, fairness, and generalization. Specifically, we introduce two novel mechanisms: Proactive Client Orchestration (PCO) and Stability-aware Model Fusion (SMF). PCO strategically guides training by evaluating each client’s potential performance gains and gradient complementarity, thereby improving overall effectiveness. SMF enhances robustness by introducing noise perturbations during local training to promote flatter minima, and it assigns aggregation weights according to model stability, thus improving both generalization and training stability. Experimental results show that FedHarmony outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods in accuracy and stability across diverse medical imaging tasks, while effectively balancing communication costs and model performance. Ablation studies further confirm the complementary benefits of PCO and SMF.

item.title: Two-Stage Privacy-Preserving Collaborative Forecasting for Wind Generation With Defense Against Malicious Eavesdroppers and Saboteurs
item.description:
IEEE Transactions on Smart Grid · Yizhi Wu, Yujian Ye, Jianxiong Hu, Xijin Guo, Guo‐Qiang Zeng, Liang Yu
Wind power generation point forecasting involves trade-offs among accuracy, privacy, attack resilience, and training efficiency. Individual forecasting (IF) protects data privacy but often suffers from limited accuracy, whereas collaborative forecasting (CF) exploits cross-farm correlations but may introduce privacy risks, malicious attacks, and high training costs. To address these challenges, this paper proposes an efficient two-stage privacy-preserving CF framework. In Stage 1, each wind farm trains an IF model independently and in parallel. In Stage 2, all farms collaboratively train a collaborative fine-tuning (CFT) model to learn IF residuals, improving forecasting accuracy while reducing the collaborative training burden. Considering two types of malicious attackers in information interaction, namely eavesdroppers and saboteurs, targeted defense mechanisms are further designed. For eavesdroppers, secure multi-party computation is embedded into the CFT process, enabling both forward and backward propagation to be performed over secret shares and preventing privacy leakage. For saboteurs, dropout-embedded self-attention and quantile regression are incorporated to mitigate the impact of tampered collaborative information and constrain abnormal residual corrections. Case studies on real-world data from 10 wind farms in Jiangsu Province, China, and the public GEFCom2014 dataset show that the proposed method achieves higher accuracy and lower collaborative training cost than federated-learning-based CF. Sensitivity analyses further reveal the effects of key defense-related parameters, providing practical guidance for parameter tuning under different security requirements.

item.title: $\mathsf {DARTIC}$: Decentralized Anonymous Reputation at Scale for Trustworthy Crowdsourcing
item.description:
IEEE Transactions on Services Computing · Mouhamed Amine Bouchiha, Mourad Rabah, Ronan Champagnat, Abdelaziz Amara Korba, Yacine M. Ghamri-Doudane
On-chain crowdsourcing leverages blockchain's decentralization, transparency, and tamper-resistance to build trustworthy and verifiable Web3 crowdsourced services. However, existing decentralized reputation frameworks do not reconcile anonymity, reputation binding, and scalability. This paper demonstrates how on-chain crowdsourcing can simultaneously achieve these requirements under a trust-minimized model. We introduce DARTIC, a decentralized, anonymous, and scalable reputation-driven framework for crowdsourcing. DARTIC presents a dual-ledger system that enables requesters and workers to use distinct pseudonyms across interactions, ensuring unlinkability while maintaining accountability. To mitigate Sybil and reputation-reset attacks, we employ zkSNARK-based set membership proofs, cryptographically binding all user pseudonyms to a single access token without revealing the linkage. For scalability, we investigate two aggregation techniques that compress multiple proofs into a single succinct proof to minimize verification overhead. In addition, we design an automated, privacy-preserving reputation model that dynamically evaluates contributions across diverse crowdsourcing contexts. To demonstrate practicality, we instantiate and assess DARTIC in both crowdsensing and federated learning scenarios. Experimental results show that (i) individual proof generation for token spending completes in less than 3s, (ii) aggregation reduces the verification time of 1024 proofs from 8.7s to 0.96s, and (iii) zk-batching lowers gas costs by more than 100x compared to a pure Layer-1 deployment. These results demonstrate that anonymity, robust reputation binding, and scalability can be jointly achieved in fully decentralized crowdsourcing systems.

item.title: FedLID: Leveraging Dimensionality to Overcome Noisy Labels in Federated Learning
item.description:
IEEE Transactions on Cloud Computing · Yufei Kang, Chenghao Hu, Baochun Li
Federated Learning (FL) facilitates multiple clients to train a shared model on their own data in a privacy-preserving manner. In real-world FL applications, clients may contain label noise due to human annotation errors. Existing methods often struggle in the presence of data heterogeneity, as they operate under the assumption that noisy data tend to produce higher losses. This assumption convolutes the distinction between hard samples and mislabeled samples, particularly in data heterogeneous environments. In this study, we comprehend the mislabeled data within the FL process by examining the dimensionality of their deep representation subspace. Our investigations reveal distinct trends in local intrinsic dimensionality between noisy and clean local samples. On the basis of this finding, we propose FedLID as a practical solution that refurbishes mislabeled data and regularizes noisy data simultaneously. Empirically, we demonstrated that FedLID surpasses current state-of-the-art methods in managing noisy labels in federated learning with data heterogeneity. Furthermore, experiments under symmetric label noise and on the large-scale CIFAR-100 dataset confirm that FedLID generalizes robustly across diverse noise types and dataset scales, showcasing the potential of subspace dimensionality in advancing data quality research.

item.title: BGSG: A Bi-Level Genetic Algorithm to Stackelberg Diagnosis Game for Edge Service Performance Monitoring
item.description:
IEEE Transactions on Cloud Computing · Shengli Pan, Kouichi Sakurai, Ying‐Chang Liang
Edge services, such as edge AI, are increasingly delivered by a federation of edge devices and edge/cloud resources that collaboratively provide edge MoE models, compute, storage, and connectivity. We abstract these collaborating units as functional links, and each service instance as a path, focusing on adversarial performance monitoring from a budgeted perspective of intelligent hybrid diagnosis choice. We formulate this challenge as a Stackelberg diagnosis game, where the operator selects a budget-feasible mixture of diagnosis schemes, while an attacker strategically allocates a constrained attack across links. To support strategy search, we propose${\sf BGSG}$, a GNN-empowered bi-level genetic algorithm framework. The GNN component acts as a topology-aware estimator built on a link–path bipartite graph, mapping diagnosis statistics and enabling amortized performance evaluation. Our theoretical discussion shows that mixed diagnosis strategies can strictly outperform pure strategies in adversarial instances and that the optimistic Stackelberg formulation is well posed under compactness and continuity. Controlled numerical evaluations on a small-scale proof-of-concept topology provide feasibility evidence for the learned diagnosis strategy and its advantage over tested baselines within this limited empirical scope; large-scale deployment validation remains future work.

item.title: Fast and Green Federated Learning: A Heterogeneity-Aware Client Selection Strategy Maximizing Overall Contribution Rate
item.description:
IEEE Transactions on Cloud Computing · Cheng Hu, Yuan Wang, Renuga Kanagavelu, Yuhui Deng, Ning Peiyan, Kangning Cai
Federated Learning is a widely studied distributed machine learning paradigm, in which numerous heterogeneous clients collaboratively train a global model without sharing their local data. The performance of Federated Learning relies on the clients involved in the training process. Some clients may contribute more than others. However, they may also require more computing resources and incur longer runtime, resulting in slower overall progress and higher energy consumption. To tackle this issue, we introduce a new concept, Contribution Rate, to better capture client contribution over a unit of time. Consequently, we propose FedRate, a novel heterogeneity-aware client selection strategy to maximize the overall contribution rate of federated learning systems. In addition, FedRate adopts a computation-efficient contribution measurement mechanism for quantifying each client’s contribution with linear complexity. Extensive experiments are conducted to evaluate FedRate against state-of-the-art baselines, under scenarios involving clients with heterogeneous computing capabilities and non-Independent and Identically Distributed (non-IID) local data. Experimental results show that FedRate significantly reduces the training time and energy consumption by an average of 51%+ and 69%+ respectively, without compromising the final accuracy of the global model.

item.title: Utility Estimation and Quality Evaluation Incentive Mechanism for Federated Learning
item.description:
IEEE Transactions on Cloud Computing · Fengsen Tian, Xinglin Zhang, Yun Li
Data across private clients in edge networks through federated learning (FL) provide crucial resources for the advancement of artificial intelligence (AI), but are often in a non-independent identically distributed (non-IID) manner. As FL clients only provide local models to the task publisher, their information asymmetry, such as training data sizes and non-IID degrees, significantly impacts on the global model accuracy. Therefore, this paper address the problems of how to make use of the clients’ training data attributes, select which clients for participating in FL, and devise reward strategies to meet economic conditions and boost engagement of high-quality clients. In particular, we propose autility-estimation andquality-evaluation (Uteque) incentive mechanism for FL. Uteque offers FL efficacy through three components: 1) data classification and publication for revealing true training data information of clients, 2) utility estimation and client selection for determining the set of clients to participate in FL, and 3) reward determination and learning quality evaluation for paying clients with truthfulness and individual rationality. This way, it evaluates the learning quality of clients solely based on their local models and formulates reward strategies based on auction theory. Extensive experiments on real-world datasets verify the effectiveness of Uteque for FL.

item.title: Optimized Multi-Scale Convolutional Neural Network-Wavelet Feature Fusion With Reinforcement-Based Explainable Selection
item.description:
IEEE Transactions on Emerging Topics in Computing · Akansha Singh, Soumendu Chakraborty, Mainak Adhikari
The escalating complexity of modern datasets demands sophisticated techniques for effective feature extraction, representation, and selection, as treating distinct data sources equally often hinders optimal performance. This study introduces a framework for Multi-Scale Feature Fusion and Adaptive Selection, transforming limited, fragmented information into meaningful insights, namely, AttenFusion-DualRL. The proposed strategy integrates a multi-stage pipeline: starting with data preprocessing for MNIST and Fashion-MNIST, followed by VGG16 feature extraction to leverage pre-trained visual knowledge. To enrich these with localized frequency information, we apply the Discrete Wavelet Transform (DWT). Subsequently, variance-based feature selection reduces dimensionality by retaining discriminative features. The core innovation lies in Cross-Domain Attention Fusion, which dynamically aligns and combines features from heterogeneous datasets. Finally, a Reinforcement Learning (RL) agent with a dual reward function optimizes feature selection by simultaneously maximizing classification accuracy, promoting sparsity, and enhancing interpretability through SHAP-guided rewards. Experiments on benchmark datasets demonstrate that the proposed strategy achieves higher classification accuracy with fewer features, showcasing improved model robustness. This approach promises significant future applications in image recognition, federated learning, and other domains that require efficient, explainable processing of diverse information sources.

item.title: Enhancing Copyright Protection in Federated Learning: A Hierarchical Watermarking Approach
item.description:
IEEE Transactions on Emerging Topics in Computing · Wei Hou, Yao Ge, Wenqiong Zhang, Y Li
Copyright protection in Federated Learning (FL) environments faces some challenges, such as fidelity, validity, robustness, and persistence, due to the large number of diverse FL clients. To address these issues, we propose a Grouped Clients Hierarchical Watermarking (GCHW) scheme, which consists of client grouping, watermark generation, watermark embedding and watermark verification. The client grouping is to group clients based on shared characteristics. In watermark generation, a hierarchical framework is proposed to establish dependencies between the group and client watermarks by embedding part of the group watermark information into each client watermark. Moreover, our GCHW scheme innovatively embeds binary watermarks into the frequency domain of model parameters at both the group and client levels during the watermark embedding phase. Experimental results demonstrate that GCHW effectively maintains fidelity and the validity of the watermarks is validated across independent and identically distributed (IID) and non-IID scenarios. GCHW also exhibits strong robustness against common attacks and defensive aggregation algorithms. In addition, GCHW shows good persistence in dynamic FL environments.

item.title: Interpretable Federated Learning for Unsupervised Video Anomaly Detection in Smart City
item.description:
IEEE Transactions on Emerging Topics in Computing · Wendong Jiang, Chih‐Yung Chang, Yu-Ting Chin, Tzu-Chia Huang, Diptendu Sinha Roy
IoT-based smart-city surveillance requires video anomaly detection (VAD) systems that can scale to massive unlabeled video streams, preserve data privacy, and operate efficiently on resource-constrained edge devices. However, existing federated-learning (FL) based VAD solutions still largely depend on costly annotations, incur high computation and communication overhead, and provide limited interpretability. To address these deployment barriers, we propose IFL-VAD-DSA, an interpretable, lightweight, and unsupervised FL framework for video anomaly detection in smart-city surveillance. First, we introduce a coarse-to-fine pseudo-labeling pipeline to eliminate the need for manual labels: a geometric modeling stage separates normal and suspicious videos at the video level, followed by a dynamic-programming sliding-window localization stage that refines pseudo-labels for precise temporal anomaly detection. Second, we design intermittent learning with variance-aware dynamic scheduling and lightweight model optimization to reduce synchronization frequency, computational burden, and communication cost, enabling efficient training on low-power IoT edge platforms. Third, we develop a transparent aggregation mechanism based on decoupled Shapley-value contribution analysis, which quantifies both individual client importance and interaction effects to improve fairness and interpretability in multi-source federated collaboration. Extensive experiments on UCF-Crime and XD-Violence demonstrate that IFL-VAD-DSA achieves state-of-the-art performance among the compared unsupervised and collaborative VAD methods, while also outperforming several weakly supervised and centralized baselines. Specifically, it reaches 88.31% and 89.64% AUC on UCF-Crime and XD-Violence in benchmark comparisons, and achieves 82.35% and 84.66% AUC under the unsupervised collaborative FL setting. These results confirm that IFL-VAD-DSA provides strong detection accuracy, improved resource efficiency, and actionable explanations of participant contributions for trustworthy smart-city surveillance.

item.title: A Robust Method for Client Selection in Dynamic MEC-Based Federated Learning
item.description:
IEEE Transactions on Vehicular Technology · Naghmeh Khajehali, Jun Hua Yan, Yang-Wai Chow, Mahdi Fahmideh
Federated learning (FL) enables collaborative model training while preserving data privacy by aggregating locally trained models from distributed clients. Client selection (CS) plays a pivotal role in the performance and scalability of FL systems. However, there is a lack of robust CS that provides balanced usage of clients for mobile edge computing (MEC) assisted FL systems and avoids unnecessary training rounds and communication. This paper presents a dual-stream robust and adaptive CS method that covers MEC nodes. The proposed method dynamically selects high-quality clients based on available resources and provides robustness against different ratio of client dropouts, adaptability to non-IID data, and effective utilization of resources, collectively enhancing the performance of FL systems and making it suitable for real-world FL deployment. Experimental evaluations using FMNIST and CIFAR-10 datasets demonstrate that the method significantly improves global model accuracy by up to 10%. In addition, it improves convergence rate (i.e., fewer communication rounds) even in high drop out client settings and reduces variance in CS performance over time compared to existing methods.

item.title: TT-Prune: Joint Model Pruning and Resource Allocation for Communication-Efficient Time-Triggered Federated Learning
item.description:
IEEE Transactions on Vehicular Technology · Xinlu Zhang, Yansha Deng, Toktam Mahmoodi
Federated learning (FL) offers new opportunities in machine learning, particularly in addressing data privacy concerns. In contrast to conventional event-based federated learning, time-triggered federated learning (TT-Fed), as a general form of both asynchronous and synchronous FL, clusters users into different tiers based on fixed time intervals. However, the FL network consists of a growing number of user devices with limited wireless bandwidth, consequently magnifying issues such as stragglers and communication overhead. In this paper, we introduce adaptive model pruning to wireless TT-Fed systems and study the problem of jointly optimizing the pruning ratio and bandwidth allocation to minimize the training loss while ensuring minimal learning latency. To answer this question, we perform convergence analysis on the gradient l_2 norm of the TT-Fed model based on model pruning. Based on the obtained convergence upper bound, a joint optimization problem of pruning ratio and wireless bandwidth is formulated to minimize the model training loss under a given delay threshold. Then, we derive closed-form solutions for wireless bandwidth and pruning ratio using Karush-Kuhn-Tucker(KKT) conditions. The simulation results show that model pruning could reduce the communication cost by 40% while maintaining the model performance at the same level.
