item.title: Edge AI-Enabled PMU Event Classification With Knowledge Distillation and Federated Learning
item.description:
IEEE Transactions on Smart Grid · Zhirui Tian, Hamed Mohsenian‐Rad, Chenye Wu
Phasor Measurement Units (PMUs) enable analysis and classification of events and abnormalities in modern power systems. However, in large and geographically dispersed networks, centralizing PMU data streams for sub-second decisions is hindered by cross-regional data-sharing restrictions, multi-layer aggregation, as well as communication delays and jitter. Purely local training at the network edge on the PMU devices themselves can avoid these bottlenecks but lacks exposure to diverse operating conditions, leading to suboptimal models. This tension calls for methods thatretain data locality and privacywhilesharing knowledge efficiently. To this end, this paper proposes an edge AI framework that integratesknowledge distillationandfederated learning, driven by the core requirement of different data-sharing constraints. First, we assume a trusted data center, where we develop a large language model-based teacher model that is fine-tuned on global data and efficiently transfers knowledge into student models trained locally via knowledge distillation. Next, we relax such an assumption and design a fair federated learning framework that exchanges gradient information among edge models while enforcing Pareto-optimal fairness to ensure stable and balanced performance. We also customize a lightweight neural network tailored for on-device deployment. With fewer than 5,000 parameters, the model adopts a compact end-to-end architecture to effectively characterize temporal dynamics and frequency-domain information in PMU time series, thereby achieving both high efficiency and strong representational capability. Experiments conducted on real-world PMU measurements demonstrate the superior performance of our framework, and ablation studies further confirm the unique contributions of each design component.

item.title: BFL-DIAS: A Blockchain and Federated Learning-Based Dynamic Identity Authentication Scheme for Industrial Internet of Things
item.description:
IEEE Transactions on Industrial Informatics · Buzhen He, Tao Feng, Xiuheng Liao, Ziang Wu, Chunhua Su
The Industrial Internet of Things requires authentication mechanisms that can adapt to dynamic contexts, preserve identity privacy, and support interoperable collaboration across security domains. This article presents BFL-DIAS, a blockchain- and federated-learning-assisted dynamic identity authentication scheme for cross-domain IIoT environments. BFL-DIAS integrates a permissioned consortium ledger, pseudonymous identity management, dynamic key and attribute-state updates, and off-path federated risk scoring into a unified workflow for registration, intradomain authentication, cross-domain authentication, and state maintenance. The federated risk score is used as a policy-assistance signal rather than as a prerequisite for cryptographic authentication, while synchronous on-chain writes are confined to registration, key update, and audit operations outside the user-facing critical path. We formalize the system and threat model and analyze the protocol under standard assumptions, showing that it provides mutual authentication, forward secrecy, impersonation resistance, replay protection, identity confidentiality, and conditional unlinkability under epoch-based pseudonym rotation. A prototype implementation on edge, mobile, and virtualized server platforms demonstrates low authentication latency, manageable ledger overhead, and stable off-path risk assessment. These results indicate that BFL-DIAS provides a secure, auditable, and deployable foundation for dynamic cross-domain authentication in industrial environments.

item.title: Range-Only SLAM: A Multihypotheses Extended Kalman Filter With Modulated Federated Information Sharing
item.description:
IEEE Transactions on Control Systems Technology · Lorenzo Bianchi, Francesco Martinelli
In this brief, we introduce a refinement to an efficient and undelayed solution proposed in the literature to solve a 2-D range-only simultaneous localization and mapping (RO-SLAM) problem. This solution consisted of stacking all the landmark hypotheses in the same extended Kalman filter (EKF) and resorting to the federated information sharing (FIS) principle to distribute the information coming from a range measurement to the different hypotheses. Pruning of hypotheses allows for reducing the computational time and obtaining a significantly better estimate with respect to the case where it is not performed, but may lead to outliers when good hypotheses are accidentally deleted from the filter. The refinement proposed in this brief improves the estimation quality, reducing at the same time the risk of the emergence of outliers, and is based on a modulation of the information sharing in the correction step of the filter, which depends on the variable to be estimated. Numerical results and experimental tests using ultra-wideband (UWB) as range sensors illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

item.title: Strong-Tracking Kalman Filter-Based Federated Learning for Distributed Fault Diagnosis
item.description:
IEEE Transactions on Systems Man and Cybernetics Systems · Lihao Ye, Ke Zhang, Bin Jiang, Silvio Simani
This article presents a federated learning framework for distributed fault diagnosis, where client updates are aggregated using a strong-tracking Kalman filter. The framework integrates robust signal-based feature extraction via wavelet packet decomposition (WPD) with a locally trained convolutional neural network (CNN). A fading-factor mechanism adapts the aggregation to sudden changes in the data and client heterogeneity, improving system stability without sharing raw data. The method is validated on two industrial case studies representative of bearing and aero-engine faults, using physically motivated, nonidentical data partitions across four clients. Against federated averaging (FedAvg), a federated proximal regularization baseline, and a sequential Kalman filter method, the proposed aggregation delivers higher diagnostic accuracy and more consistent performance on the most imbalanced client. Evidence is reported through accuracy tables, receiver-operating characteristics, and confusion matrices, with results showing shorter departures from nominal behavior and improved global consistency. This framework provides a practical solution for reliable, privacy-preserving fault diagnosis under realistic data heterogeneity.

item.title: BadPromptFL: Parameters-Free Backdoor Attack on Vision-Language Federated Learning
item.description:
IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems for Video Technology · Maozhen Zhang, Mengnan Zhao, Wei Wang, Tianhang Zheng, Bo Wang
Prompt-based tuning has emerged as a lightweight alternative to full fine-tuning in large vision-language models, enabling efficient adaptation via learned contextual prompts. This paradigm has recently been extended to federated learning settings, where clients collaboratively train prompts under data privacy constraints. However, the security implications of prompt-based aggregation in federated multimodal learning remain largely underexplored, leaving this paradigm vulnerable to prompt-space attacks. In this paper, we introduceBadPromptFL, the first model-parameter-free backdoor attack specifically targeting prompt-based federated learning in vision-language models. Instead of manipulating model weights, BadPromptFL introduces a parameter-free alternating optimization mechanism where malicious clients jointly update stealthy visual triggers and local prompt embeddings to force malicious alignment in the contrastive latent space. Through private collusion, these clients construct a coherent global trigger, crafting poisoned prompts that remain statistically similar to benign ones to covertly hijack the global prompt aggregation process. By jointly optimizing image perturbations with prompts,BadPromptFLactivates the backdoor in a manner that is highly effective and difficult to detect. Additionally, we demonstrate that the injected backdoor achieves reliable convergence within the federated learning framework, explaining why malicious prompt updates can be incorporated into the global prompt without causing divergent training behavior. By leveraging the contextual learning behavior of CLIP-style architectures,BadPromptFLdelivers high attack success rates (e.g., > 90%) with minimal visibility and limited client participation. Extensive experiments on multiple benchmarks and aggregation settings further validate the effectiveness, stealth, and adaptability of our method, revealing important security risks in prompt-based federated learning systems. Our code is available athttps://github.com/Maozhen-Zhang/BadPromptFL.git

item.title: Density-Aware Adaptive Weight Optimization Against Data Heterogeneity in Federated Learning
item.description:
IEEE Transactions on Artificial Intelligence · Sheng Gao, Chen Huang, Jianming Zhu, X Y Ma, Jin Dong
Federated learning (FL) provides a privacy-preserving framework for distributed model training across decentralized participating clients (PCs). However, its performance is significantly hindered by data heterogeneity, where non-independent and identically distributed (non-IID) data across PCs induce client drift, compromise model generalization, and may even impede convergence. Although various optimization schemes have been proposed to alleviate these issues, they still suffer from slow convergence and insufficient generalization. In this article, we propose FedWeight, a novel density-aware adaptive weight optimization in FL that effectively mitigates data heterogeneity without relying on auxiliary data or historical parameters. Specifically, FedWeight allows each client to dynamically and adaptively adjust the loss function weights based on class-wise density derived from kernel density estimation. By assigning larger weights to sparse classes, FedWeight balances learning across sparse and dense classes, thereby accelerating convergence and improving generalization under non-IID settings. Finally, theoretical analysis and extensive experimental results demonstrate that FedWeight achieves more accurate models and significantly faster convergence, improving the performance of integrated baseline approaches.

item.title: Collaborative Knowledge Editing for Large Language Model Services in Edge-Cloud Computing
item.description:
IEEE Transactions on Services Computing · Guozeng Xu, Xiuhua Li, Junhao Wen, Qiang He, Xiaofei Wang, Victor C. M. Leung
With the rapid deployment of large language model (LLM) technology across various fields, numerous LLMs have been deployed on edge servers (ESs) to provide low-latency generative services for edge devices. However, as factual knowledge evolves, the massive number of parameters in LLMs poses significant challenges for updating LLMs on ESs. Existing studies employ federated fine-tuning to update LLMs, but these unconstrained updating approaches can lead to overfitting and knowledge forgetting, while also resulting in substantial overhead. Knowledge editing (KE), as a promising technology, ensures the injection of new knowledge while preserving existing knowledge by editing specific parameters. In this paper, we propose multi-ES collaborative KE for the first time and design the CoKE and pCoKE frameworks in edge-cloud scenarios. These frameworks enhance editing efficiency by extracting identical expressions of the same knowledge across different LLM parameters for collaborative editing across multiple ESs. Additionally, we incorporate a personalized selection module in pCoKE to provide domain-specific generative services on ESs. To further reduce editing latency, we design a binary search-based resource allocation algorithm to balance editing latency across ESs. Extensive experiments demonstrate that CoKE and pCoKE reduce editing latency by 73% while maintaining high editing quality. Moreover, pCoKE achieves an approximately 6% improvement in editing quality.

item.title: TFRL-MD: Transformer-Enhanced Federated Reinforcement Learning for Intelligent Microservice Deployment and Resource Allocation
item.description:
IEEE Transactions on Cloud Computing · Keli Liu, Jie Yang, Xiaoli Ruan, Yuehua Chen, Xu Wang, Jianhong Cheng
Edge computing provides low-latency execution environments for delay-sensitive microservices by deploying computational resources at the network periphery. However, microservice deployment and resource allocation in geographically distributed, heterogeneous edge environments must simultaneously navigate challenges such as data privacy preservation, heterogeneous resource constraints, and dynamic workload fluctuations. Therefore, we propose TFRL-MD, a Transformer-enhanced federated reinforcement learning framework for privacy-preserving and intelligent microservice deployment and resource allocation. The framework models each edge node as an independent Actor-Critic agent to learn deployment policies via local training, enabling cross-node collaborative optimization without sharing raw environmental data. To improve the quality of knowledge fusion among heterogeneous edge nodes, we design a Transformer-based Embedding-Space Aggregation Mechanism (EASM) that leverages multi-head self-attention to adaptively fuse their intermediate-layer knowledge representations. Furthermore, a dual-channel hybrid objective training mechanism is constructed to synchronously inject the aggregated global representations into the optimization targets of both Actor and Critic networks as differentiable semantic embeddings, thereby smoothly guiding local gradient descent and eliminating the policy oscillations inherent in traditional parameter overwriting.Dynamic simulation experiments, conducted using the EUA dataset from the Australian Central Business District (CBD) region, demonstrate that TFRL-MD outperforms various baselines in both average response time and load balancing, achieving maximum improvements of 46.01% and 61.11%, respectively.

item.title: KF4FL: Kalman Filtering for Privacy-Preserving Federated Learning With Momentum
item.description:
IEEE Transactions on Industrial Informatics · Xuebin Ren, Qing Han, Shusen Yang, Yuqian Yang
Federated learning (FL) empowers numerous industrial applications by analyzing tremendous data from distributed smart devices. To reduce communication costs and training delays, momentum-based optimizers are often adopted in FL for training acceleration. Meanwhile, considering frequent model exchange in FL, differential privacy (DP) is also utilized to provide a rigorous privacy guarantee. Therefore, it is promising to combine momentum-based FL with DP for achieving efficient and private FL. However, besides impacting the FL model utility, the added noise would also exacerbate the overshoot issue in momentum-based FL optimization. To this end, we propose KF4FL, a DP-enhanced and momentum-accelerated FL framework by exploring the application of Kalman filter (KF), which can achieve both high model utility and stable FL training without compromising the privacy guarantee. Specifically, KF4FL is a two-fold KF scheme consisting of a gradient noise filtering for reducing the impact of noise in model utility, and a parameter overshoot filtering for stability enhancement in momentum-based training. Besides, by adapting the KF variant of Kalman-consensus information filter, we further propose KF4FL+, an efficient extension of KF4FL in the decentralized FL setting. Extensive experiments demonstrate that KF4FL can reduce up to 5$\%$accuracy loss and 20$\%$convergence time than the state-of-the-art methods. KF4FL+ further improves consensus efficiency by 10$\%$under sparse network topologies.

item.title: Enhancing Early Mortality Prediction With Clinical Notes as Time-Series Scores
item.description:
IEEE Transactions on Human-Machine Systems · Gabriel Vázquez-Serrano, Maite Oronoz, Alicia Pérez
The optimization of early mortality prediction models to accurately identify high-risk patients during a hospital admission is key in medical research to assist in healthcare decision-making. While these models use structured (physiological features) or unstructured (free-text clinical notes) data, integrating them synergistically, especially for early prediction, remains a challenge. We introduce a novel, model-agnostic approach to represent clinical notes as quantitative, task-specific time-series, structurally aligning them with physiological features. Instead of relying on complex multimodal architectures, we shift fusion from the architecture level to the data level by transforming each note into a numerical mortality risk score, creating a new time-series feature that can be seamlessly integrated into any standard time-series prediction model. We evaluate our approach on the following: first, early prediction, second, data scalability, and third, versatility across centralized, federated, and local learning frameworks, in an attempt to assess the stability of the approach in scenarios with different amounts of data to learn from. Using only readily accessible data from the first 8–24 h postadmission, our method significantly boosts baseline model performance, with relative improvements of up to 7 % in area under the receiver operating characteristic curve and 28 % in area under the precision–recall curve over prior work on early prediction that relies solely on physiological data. Moreover, we find that incorporating our text-derived scores significantly achieves higher performance gains than nearly doubling the training data size in scenarios where no textual information is considered. Rather than proposing a predictive model, we present a new technique to structure clinical narratives, enabling a more effective fusion with temporal, quantitative health data for improved early prediction of mortality.

item.title: P 3 Forecast: Personalized and Adaptive Cloud Workload Prediction via GAN-Based Federated Data Augmentation
item.description:
IEEE Transactions on Parallel and Distributed Systems · Xin Yong, Yan Li, Yu Kuang, Zhuozhao Li, Chao Qun Shen, Xingwei Wang
To comply with privacy regulations and self-protection from cloud outages, increasingly more users are leveraging multiple cloud providers for service deployment. However, due to the isolation of highly Non-Identically and Independently Distributed (Non-IID) workload datasets and deficiencies of existing methods as reflected in our experimental studies, no cloud providers can single-handedly capture the workload patterns of such users for accurate workload prediction. Accordingly, we proposeP3Forecast, aPersonalizedPrivacy-Preserving Cloud workload prediction framework based on Federated Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs), which allows cloud providers with Non-IID workload data to collaboratively train workload prediction models as preferred while protecting privacy. We first design a data synthesis quality assessment method based on Dynamic Time Warping (calledpattern-aware DTW), which is insusceptible to time series length and reliable for the comparison of temporal patterns. By usingpattern-aware DTWas the model aggregation weights, we adopt the Federated Learning (FL) of a GAN model for the augmentation of IID workload training datasets per cloud provider. Then, we further design a post-training method of local workload prediction models, which consists of a query mechanism based on comprehensive evaluation of data synthesis informativeness and an adaptive learning rate adjustment strategy for stable convergence. Extensive experiments driven by real-world workloads demonstrate that compared with the state-of-the-art,P3Forecastimproves workload prediction accuracy by 23.7%-64.5% on average over all cloud providers, while ensuring the fastest convergence in Federated GAN training.

item.title: Digital Twin for Multitimescale Economic Dispatch in Cyber-Physical Energy Systems
item.description:
IEEE Transactions on Industrial Informatics · Jiaqi Tian, Bonan Huang, Tianyi Li, Wenzhong Gao, Zhongming Yao, Yumeng Song
Cyber-physical energy systems (CPESs) involve multitimescale decision-making to balance short- and long-term dispatch requirements. However, existing distributed economic dispatch methods typically emphasize either short-term optimality or long-term predictive capability but rarely achieve both simultaneously. To address this issue, we propose a digital twin (DT)-empowered framework, model, and method for multitimescale economic dispatch (MTED) in CPESs. First, we design a two-layer MTED framework that integrates a physical layer and a DT layer. The DT layer consists of individual DTs, which serve as virtual replicas of the physical components in the physical layer, and a federated DT that coordinates the interactions among these individual DTs. Second, we formulate the MTED problem in CPESs as a complex optimization problem that involves both nonconvex and convex decision variables, related to long and short timescales, respectively. Third, we propose a federated MuZero-Newton-descent method to solve the MTED problem. By using this method, we can make the short-term optimal decision while ensuring long-term predictive capability for planning. Finally, simulations demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

item.title: From Stochastic Conjugate Gradient to Stochastic Second-Order Optimization, Driven by Conjugate Coefficient With Second-Order Information
item.description:
IEEE Transactions on Neural Networks and Learning Systems · Zhuang Yang
Conjugate gradient (CG) and second-order information (SOI) receive increasing interest due to their crucial role in improving stochastic first-order (SFO) algorithms for solving machine learning problems. Although a variety of stochastic CG (SCG) and stochastic second-order (SSO) algorithms were studied, nearly all works only focus on either empirical or theoretical aspects for specific tasks by using SFO algorithms with CG or SOI separately. Thus, it is desired to explore the effect of the combination of CG and SOI on SFO algorithms. To cope with this issue, we develop a type of fast and low-cost SSO conjugate gradient (S2CG) algorithms, extending the family of SCG and SSO algorithms. Prior to our work, second-order CG methods only apply CG to solve the suboptimization problem, such as the (quasi-)Newton equation, which is time-consuming for large-scale optimization problems or problems requiring high-precision solutions. We show that the transition from SCG to SSO is driven by the conjugate coefficient with SOI. Moreover, we provide theoretical guarantees of different S2CG algorithms for strongly convex, general convex, and Polyak-Łojasiewicz (PL) cases. Finally, extensive experiments on different machine learning tasks, covering support vector machine (SVM), logistic regression (LR), federated learning (FL), and neural networks (NNs), significantly validate the superiority and robustness of S2CG algorithms over state-of-the-art SFO, SCG, and SSO algorithms.

item.title: Range Penalization: Theoretical Insights With Applications in Federated Learning
item.description:
IEEE Transactions on Information Theory · Yiyuan She, Zhaojun Hu, Yifan Sun
This paper introduces range regularization for federated learning with linear systematic components to enhance statistical accuracy and induce cross-client regularity conducive to quantization, coding, and resource efficiency. Our approach identifies features with shared weights across different clients and adaptively clusters the weights of personalized features at extreme values, a process we refer to as polar clustering. Theoretical analysis of the associated estimators poses significant challenges due to the seminorm nature and non-decomposability of the regularizer. We develop new proof techniques for the nonasymptotic analysis of statistical accuracy and faithful pattern recovery. Moreover, a fast optimization algorithm that leverages varying degrees of local strong convexity is proposed to reduce iteration complexity. Experiments support the efficacy and efficiency of the proposed approach.

item.title: Computing Scheme for Space–Air–Ground Integrated Edge Computing Networks: A Reputation Blockchain-Enabled FRL Approach
item.description:
IEEE Transactions on Vehicular Technology · Sicheng Liu, Wenxiao Shi, Xue Wang, Fengye Hu
Space-air-ground integrated edge computing (SAGI-EC) networks have emerged as a novel architecture due to seamless connectivity, flexible deployment, and scalable resources. However, existing studies mainly focus on computing strategies, while challenges such as low node cooperation willingness and poor device reliability hinder the adoption of SAGI-EC. To address these challenges, we first propose a heterogeneous SAGI-EC framework that incorporates a reputation blockchain. Then, a multi-weight subjective logic model and an adaptive interaction weight updating method are employed to achieve accurate reputation evaluation and dynamic management. In addition, a problem is formulated to minimize the weighted sum of total time delay and energy consumption. By modeling the computing process as a Markov decision process and solving it through a federated reinforcement learning (FRL) approach, we propose a space-air-ground integrated edge computing algorithm based on a reputation incentive mechanism and FRL (RFSIEC). Simulation results indicate that our proposed scheme can effectively suppress and filter unreliable devices, significantly reducing the average total time delay and energy consumption while improving the task success rate.

item.title: Federated Learning With Integrated Sensing, Communication, and Computation: FedSGD-ISCC or FedAVG-ISCC
item.description:
IEEE Transactions on Vehicular Technology · Yipeng Liang, Qimei Chen, Dingzhu Wen, Guangxu Zhu, Muhammad Kaleem Awan, Mingming Zhao
With the integration of sensing, communication, and computation (ISCC) emerging as a key paradigm for 6G, feder ated learning (FL) with ISCC (FL-ISCC) provides a promising solution to enhance training efficiency by orchestrating sample collection, local model updating, and wireless exchange. This work focuses on two core FL-ISCC algorithms: Federated Av eraging (FedAVG)-ISCC and Federated Stochastic Gradient De scent (FedSGD)-ISCC. Although both are widely used, their com parative performance and theoretical characterization remain inadequately explored. To address this, we establish a general FL ISCC framework and conduct a comprehensive theoretical and experimental analysis. Our main contributions include deriving the convergence rates for both algorithms under realistic network conditions, accounting for data heterogeneity and communication errors. The analysis reveals that FedAVG-ISCC achieves higher accuracy under independent and identically distributed (IID) data, while FedSGD-ISCC exhibits stronger robustness in non IID and error-prone wireless environments. These theoretical findings are corroborated by numerical simulations, providing actionable insights for selecting and deploying FL algorithms in practical ISCC systems.

item.title: HealthEngine: An Integrated Healthcare Analytics Model Using Multimodal Transformer, Deep Multitask Neural Networks, and SHAP
item.description:
IEEE Transactions on Computational Social Systems · Moshedayan Sirapangi, S. Gopikrishnan, Norbert Herencsár, Meng Li, Gautam Srivastava
The development of more accurate and explainable health predictions is paramount in view of the increasing prevalence rates of chronic diseases and mental illnesses. Existing methods often under-utilize the rich, heterogeneous data streams coming from wearable devices, environmental sensors, and behavioral data, and hence fall short in making predictions that are both accurate and actionable. Most models lack transparency and cannot avoid privacy concerns due to the samples used from sensitive health data. This study specifically addresses the challenge of building a predictive healthcare framework capable of handling multimodal data, data streams that originate from different modalities (physiological, behavioral, and environmental), and exhibit intrinsic heterogeneity. Unlike general heterogeneous datasets, multimodal health data demands models that can effectively integrate structured, semistructured, and temporal information while ensuring privacy and interpretability. In this work, we propose an integrated comprehensive multimodal health prediction framework with five advanced methods, namely multimodal transformer networks (MTN), deep multitask neural networks (DMNN), Shapley additive explanations (SHAP) based explainability, Federated Learning, and Bayesian neural networks (BNN). MTN uses attention mechanisms to fuse different data modalities and captures cross-modal dependencies effectively, achieving an improvement of 8% to 12% in prediction accuracy. DMNN leverages multitask learning to share knowledge between related health prediction tasks, reducing error rates by 10%–15%. SHAP is used to provide localized, patient-specific explanations that improve clinical trust by up to 85%. This is done by privately training the models on decentralized datasets, which provides results without more than a 3% drop in precision compared with centralized models. Third, BNNs are used to quantify uncertainty in predictions, providing useful confidence intervals that improve clinical decision-making by 20%. The results obtained suggest significant improvements in predictive accuracy, transparency, and privacy preservation. This research not only improves health predictions through multimodal analysis but also tackles significant limitations in privacy, interpretability, and uncertainty quantification, thus promoting informed clinical decisions and customized patient care.

item.title: Unifying Personalization and Generalization in Federated Few-Shot Learning via Complementary Collaboration
item.description:
IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems for Video Technology · Shanfeng Wang, Ke Liu, Zhengyi Dong, Jianzhao Li, Yuan Gao, Maoguo Gong
Personalized federated few-shot learning offers a promising approach to develop customized models for each client while respecting privacy constraints and decentralized data, addressing the challenge of limited labeled sample. However, existing methods prioritize strong personalization for seen classes under extreme data scarcity, but they struggle with weaker generalization to unseen classes under non-IID conditions, which severely restrict their practical utility. To circumvent this problem, we propose a novel personalized federated few-shot learning framework that integrates two levels of complementary learning to simultaneously improve personalization and generalization in such challenging settings. At the intra-client level, a dual-branch architecture is proposed with a global branch capturing holistic image semantics and a local branch focusing on fine-grained features from random crops. These branches interact via knowledge distillation and leverage the synergy between global context and local details to enable robust representation learning from scarce data. At the inter-client level, we propose a collaborative aggregation strategy that prioritizes partners with maximally complementary feature distributions. By integrating knowledge from both similar and diverse clients quantified by maximum mean discrepancy-based prototype discrepancy, our approach effectively leverages cross-federation information. This dual-level strategy ensures strong personalization for seen classes and robust generalization to unseen classes. Experiments on benchmark datasets confirm the effectiveness of our proposed method.

item.title: FedDD: Combating Federated Noisy Label Learning With Intra- and Inter-Distributional Difference
item.description:
IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems for Video Technology · Tong Jin, Chen-Chen Zong, Sheng-Jun Huang
Federated learning (FL) enables multiple parties to collaboratively train a global machine learning model without sharing local data. While FL has made awe-inspiring advances, most existing studies assume fully clean data labels on clients, which rarely holds in real-world scenarios where label noise is prevalent and detrimental to FL performance. Prior approaches typically rely on the small-loss criterion to identify noisy instances, which has been proven to struggle in highly heterogeneous settings. To overcome this, we propose a robust framework called FedDD that tackles label noise in FL by leveraging intra-and inter-distributional differences. Instead, FedDD employs an intra-difference measure, which utilizes the intra-logit variance to preliminarily identify the clean subset. Subsequently, it refines the data by introducing an inter-distributional difference metric based on prediction discrepancies between local and global models. To further utilize identified noisy examples, a novel federated semi-supervised learning paradigm is proposed that amalgamates knowledge from the global and local models to guide pseudo-labeling. Extensive experiments on benchmark datasets under both independent and identically distributed (IID) and non-IID settings demonstrate the superiority of FedDD over state-of-the-art methods.

item.title: Energy-Efficient Federated Edge Computing for Predictive Scheduling in Vehicular Networks
item.description:
IEEE Transactions on Vehicular Technology · Xiangjie Kong, Kaiyu Zhang, Zhenhui Xu, Junjie Zhou, Guojiang Shen, Amr Kamal Rabea Tolba
Dynamic vehicular networks suffer from unstable connections, fluctuating bandwidth, and high mobility, leading to energy-intensive and redundant federated learning (FL) updates. Conventional reactive scheduling methods fail to predict short lived connections or sudden traffic surges, resulting in inefficient resource utilization. To address these challenges, we propose EcoFed, a novel energy-efficient framework that integrates predictive scheduling with adaptive model compression in a closed loop architecture. EcoFed employs a communication-aware re inforcement learning scheduler to optimize client selection by anticipating connectivity issues and low-contribution clients. It incorporates a dynamic FL strategy with a knowledge transfer mechanism to compress model updates based on real-time net work conditions. Additionally, a lightweight Transformer-based prediction module forecasts client connectivity and workload patterns to enable proactive scheduling. Experimental results demonstrate that EcoFed significantly reduces energy consumption and achieves competitive latency by intelligently trading off latency for energy savings under heavy loads. The framework accelerates model convergence across diverse vehicular scenarios, including multi-modal tasks, while maintaining high prediction accuracy. It also ensures robust performance under network disruptions and scales effectively. The framework supports privacy-preserving updates for 6G-driven vehicle-to-everything applications, outperforming state-of-the-art methods in intelligent transportation systems.

item.title: Sequential Knowledge Distillation Federated Learning With D2D Communication in VANETs
item.description:
IEEE Transactions on Vehicular Technology · Fan‐Hsun Tseng, Yu-Hsiang Huang
In vehicular ad-hoc networks (VANETs), a centralized infrastructure such as a base station or roadside unit can collect data from vehicles on both highways and surface streets, but this causes heavy communications. Vehicles can train a model cooperatively by using the federated learning (FL) framework for collaborative learning tasks, e.g., route planning, platoon lane-change prediction, and crash risk prediction, but still suffer from centralized communications in VANETs. To address the challenge, the paper proposes the sequential knowledge distillation federated learning (SKDFL) framework. The SKDFL framework reduces communication cost and the infrastructure's load in vehicular networks by leveraging device-to-device (D2D) communication and sequential model training. Within the SKDFL, the proposed deadline-driven upload strategy with brain floating-point (Bfloat16)-based model compression is introduced to further reduce communication cost. To mitigate the data heterogeneity of diverse vehicular devices, SKDFL integrates a vehicular device selection strategy and sequential knowledge distillation learning, enabling models to progressively absorb diverse knowledge from various vehicles. In addition, a direction guidance of D2D communication mechanism is introduced to enable more vehicles to participate in training before the upload deadline under network and computational heterogeneity. Compared with conventional FL methods, the results show that SKDFL improves model accuracy by 1.71% to 2.15% under non-IID data scenarios while reducing communication costs by more than 50%, measured by the number of uploads and data transfer size.
